doc.title: Peter Vacher interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001

title: British jazz writers and magazines
summary: British and French writers took the music seriously; Vacher names Jazz Journal, Jazz Monthly and key figures like McCarthy and Delaunay.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: We were very fortunate. There was a number of writers who I think in a way, this is a difficult claim, seemed to take the music more seriously than their American counterparts. You know you have people like Panassié in France and Charles Delaunay. And in London you had Sinclair Traill who founded Jazz Journal, you had Max Jones, you had Charles Fox, you had Albert McCarthy. These are major people in terms of documenting the music. Albert McCarthy along with Charles Delaunay were the first discographers. There were good magazines to write for. So quite early on I was getting into magazines which were magazines of quality. And it was principally because of these key people, particularly, as I say, Max of the Melody Maker, and then Albert McCarthy with Jazz Monthly, which was a fine magazine, a bit on the lines of the Jazz Review, Nat Hentoff’s thing.
